mechanism_narrative: Transit station footfall is the earliest observable proxy for discretionary trip-making. TRANSIT has risen 8.2 points off its t-2w trough (-47.9 to -39.7) while RETAIL_REC rose 7.0 points over the same span. Continued transit recovery pulls shoppers back into retail and recreation venues, lifting the forward 28-day mean above the trailing one.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -47.9 at t-2w to -39.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Forward 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing 28-day mean of -45.5 despite TRANSIT continuing to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility anchors weekday retail footfall in Manhattan. WORKPLACES has rebounded 5.8 points from its t-2w trough of -50.4 but remains stuck at -44.6, essentially flat versus t-1w. Once the weekly WORKPLACES mean crosses above -45.5, commuter-driven lunchtime and after-work retail demand resumes, pushing the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean higher.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean crosses above -45.5 (it sits at -44.6 at t-0w after -44.9 at t-1w)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 5.8 points from the t-2w trough
regime_hint: post-trough stabilization with offices partially repopulating
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean falls below the trailing mean even after WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly means above -45.5.

mechanism_narrative: Households substitute between staying home and going out. RESIDENTIAL has eased from +11.4 to +10.0 while PARKS recovered from -24.3 to -7.0. The joint move - less home confinement plus more outdoor activity - signals a re-engagement with out-of-home consumption that spills over into retail and recreation trips over the next fortnight.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +10.5 while PARKS weekly mean is above -10.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from +11.4 to +10.0 while PARKS rose from -24.3 to -7.0
regime_hint: reopening with in-home work still elevated
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is lower than its trailing mean in weeks where RESIDENTIAL is below +10.5 and PARKS is above -10.0 simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy trips are the routine, near-daily mobility that never fully shut down. GROCERY_PHARM has improved from -22.9 to -14.4, a 8.5-point recovery, and historically leads broader retail re-engagement by roughly one week because routine errands rebuild the habit of in-person shopping. This pulls RETAIL_REC up within seven days.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered 8.5 points from -22.9 at t-2w to -14.4 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with essential-activity baseline intact
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no week-on-week gain in the next 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM improves for two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS is the most weather-sensitive series in the catalog. Its 17.3-point swing from -24.3 to -7.0 while transit and workplaces barely moved indicates a lengthening-daylight, warming-weather seasonal shift rather than a policy change. Seasonally-driven outdoor traffic converts into errand and recreation stops, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds -10.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved 17.3 points between t-2w and t-0w while WORKPLACES moved only 5.8 points from its trough
regime_hint: spring seasonal transition with outdoor-permissive weather
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is at or below the trailing mean while PARKS holds above -10.0 for two straight weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: Any visible rebound in retail and recreation footfall is the trigger for pre-emptive restriction reimposition, because rising RETAIL_REC is read as compliance decay. RETAIL_REC has already climbed 7.0 points from -48.9 to -41.9. If it crosses -40.0, authorities tighten capacity rules and the forward 28-day mean falls back below the trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 7.0 points from -48.9 at t-2w to -41.9 at t-0w
regime_hint: renewed restriction tightening triggered by rebound signals
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC sustains weekly means above -40.0 for three consecutive weeks without the forward 28-day mean dropping below the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: A persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL reading of roughly +10 with WORKPLACES pinned near -44.6 defines a durable work-from-home equilibrium. Under that equilibrium the retail recovery is capped: discretionary trips occur but at home-office-substituted volumes, so the marginal uptick stalls and the forward 28-day mean slips below the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above +10.0 while WORKPLACES stays at or below -44.5
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has held between +10.0 and +11.4 across all four weeks while WORKPLACES moved only 0.4 points between t-1w and t-0w
regime_hint: entrenched work-from-home regime with office density capped
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean exceeds the trailing mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10.0 and WORKPLACES remains below -44.5.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have decoupled: transit gained 8.2 points off its trough while workplace mobility gained only 0.8 points over the same two weeks. Transit trips that are not commute trips are discretionary - shopping, dining, recreation - so the divergence implies RETAIL_REC demand is rebuilding faster than office return, supporting a higher forward mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean exceeds WORKPLACES weekly mean by more than 3.0 points (current gap: 4.9)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -39.7 versus WORKPLACES at -44.6 at t-0w, a 4.9-point gap
regime_hint: partial reopening where discretionary travel outpaces commuting
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean is at or below the trailing mean whenever the TRANSIT-minus-WORKPLACES gap exceeds 3.0 points.
